answer: Each agent key gets voting weight only after its owner locks scarce collateral, and the contract caps how much one owner can lock into a single decision. A sybil attacker can mint thousands of keys, but cannot multiply influence without splitting and locking more capital; that capital stays unavailable and may be slashed if the vote violates the protocol. The island of keys is therefore less important than the costly stake beneath them, though velvet and terrace identities add no weight on their own.
